reason: The talk states the coins scatter across an enormous number of dies that almost never link, and explicitly kills a tight cluster, any minting-order chain, and any local imitation.

The second hoard is raised because it came up still in its jar with packing intact, 'the very context our hoard lost'; its recovery is called every bit as hurried, its latest coins decades apart, and its contents a type-for-type mirror.
He rejects Teodorescu, saying worn-beside-fresh coins are a household's two-generation accumulation; the talk denies sorting by weight and insists on one deposit buried once.
The record shows a multi-week reversal in each of the three years; season made no difference, the final year was as strong as the first, and the disturbances ran weeks not days.

The logbooks are cited for 'one narrow reason' — a skipper's note dated the sensor failure; catch totals are called too noisy, the site was picked off a chart, and nothing suggests the crews noticed the reversals.
The stated plan is a cabled station paired with a spring ship survey; the moorings come up for good, the station goes on exactly the same spot, and the series stays in-house.
She accepts the nutrient claim but rests it on plankton blooms, calling the sediment traps indifferent to the flow and the rivers far too small.
All four cliffs stayed in use with the old rotation and no crowding, never any canopy bedding; only the arrival time shifted to after dark.

She says Deren has it backwards — the wariness he treats as driver is a product of the disturbance; the talk also states the model was built on forest species, has thinner evidence, and never fit season one.
The 'real limit' is uneven habituation leaving the shyest groups thin; parallel teams gave same-day comparisons, notches stayed legible, and both seasons fell in the same fruiting year.
Crews set out rows of quick-growing figs along the roadcut; the road stays open at all hours, no second survey was ordered, and no reserve status was proposed.
He says the payment 'for computing the cuttings' is the whole of his point; the ledgers record no instrument purchases, place her on the western line, and survive because the fire never reached them.
The binding — nineteenth-century, far younger than the pages — is what settled the dating; watermarks told nothing, no datable structure is named, and the ink is uniform throughout.

He accepts Odile's objection and cites the notebooks' own doubtful hill pages; commissions did hire the shortcut for upland work, contemporaries got steep ground right, and the hill surveys miss badly.
The notebooks passed to a schoolmaster at Aubrec who taught from them thirty years; they were never separated, are documented in every decade, and Dole left no heirs.
Two dyestuffs indicate a repair campaign generations after weaving; the madder is the local strain, no purple drift, and both reds are true dyes in the thread.

He describes it because it won a prize and no conservator would defend it now — 'how fast this field moves'; the adhesive is gone, the photos add nothing new, and the paperwork never mentions discoloration.
Stains lifted evenly but a tide line crept in and needed a second pass; the shielded fibers tested no different and the corner drapes as softly as the rest.
He calls the matter settled by the 1961 loan agreement, with preference irrelevant; the parish promised nothing about display, the church stays dry, and his lab was never consulted.
The evenings' 'real work was survival', keeping ballads sung after emigration; no broadsides were found, farm versions stayed distinct, and the gatherings date back to the 1740s.
The recasting fact is the descendants' written petition; the contracts are silent on publication, the archive consulted beyond the estate, and the wax's good condition is no part of the argument.
The striking thing is absence — dozens of notebook songs were never recorded; where both survive they match word for word, her texts carry every refrain, and every listed singer is a distinct voice.
The post is 'a boundary and nothing else', past which the coastal stock takes over; its ledgers record goods not travelers, officers never sang, and both visits are dated in her diary.
What the plates uniquely hold is the late snowbeds absent from the written notes; the markers all stood, he shot in early July, and the ledges show untrodden.
It sits where mapped on the ledges but has vanished from the scree; plants are no larger and flower as freely, the upper limit outran the models, and there are no scree seedlings.
He agrees about the crest but says valley losses track 1970s drainage channels, so the report cannot stand whole; grazing is called a dead end and Elde's records complete.
The worry is the proposed cable-car corridor crossing the upper plots before anyone returns; the grant was renewed, a return is planned within five years, and the park declined to adopt the transect.
